mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 2 Series M240i engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 2 Series M240i engine replacement typically costs between £2,800 and £5,200 depending on the condition (used, reconditioned, or rebuilt) and the specific engine code. Used engines start from around £1,800, reconditioned units from £2,800, and fully rebuilt engines with a 12-month warranty from £3,000. Labour for supply and fit adds approximately £800-£1,500 depending on the workshop. Main dealer replacement costs can exceed £4,200.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of oil filter housing failure in a BMW 2 Series M240i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common symptoms are coolant loss without visible external leaks, oil contamination (milky appearance), and a sweet smell from the engine bay. The B58's plastic oil filter housing is prone to cracking, which can lead to oil and coolant mixing - a known potentially catastrophic problem. If left unchecked, this can cause bearing failure and engine seizure.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 2 Series M240i?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the vehicle's value and the extent of the damage. For an F22 M240i (2017-2021) worth £18,000-£28,000, a reconditioned engine at £2,800-£3,800 is often worthwhile if you plan to keep the car. For G42 models (2021+) worth £25,000-£45,000, replacement is almost always justified. If the car is worth under £5,000, a used engine or repair may be more cost-effective.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 2 Series M240i engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical BMW 2 Series M240i engine replacement takes 3-5 working days from order to completion, assuming the engine is in stock. Supply-only orders are usually dispatched within 1-2 working days. Supply and fit through our specialist network typically takes 3-5 days, including delivery, fitting, and ECU calibration.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the M235i and the M240i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The BMW M235i (2014-2016) uses the N55 3.0-litre inline-six producing 326hp, while the M240i (2017-2021) uses the newer B58 3.0-litre inline-six producing 335-340hp. The M240i replaced the M235i in the F22/F23 generation. The G42 M240i (2021-present) uses an updated B58 producing 374hp.

mainEntity.name: Will a replacement BMW 2 Series M240i engine pass the MoT?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - all engines supplied through EnginesMarket are MoT emissions compliant. Rebuilt and reconditioned engines are tested to ensure they meet the original emissions standards for the vehicle's year. For M240i models with OPF (Otto Particulate Filter), compliance is confirmed before dispatch.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 2 Series M240i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 2 Series M240i arrived in 2017 as the replacement for the M235i, bringing BMW's new modular B58 3.0-litre inline-six turbo engine to the F22 Coupe and F23 Convertible. The M240i badge represented a significant step up in performance, with the B58 delivering 335-340hp compared to the M235i's 326hp N55. The G42 generation M240i (2021-present) took performance to another level with 374hp from an updated B58.

milestones.description: B58B30M0, 3.0L turbo inline-six, 335-340hp, 500Nm (F22 Coupe, F23 Convertible launch, replaced N55)
B58B30O1, 3.0L turbo inline-six, 374hp, 500Nm (G42 Coupe launch, xDrive standard in many markets)

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the BMW 2 Series M240i is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: BMW 2 Series M240i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: H3 (intro, 2-3 sentences): The BMW 2 Series M240i has been powered by two generations of 3.0-litre inline-six engines: the earlier N55 (2014-2016 M235i) and the B58 (2017-present M240i). The N55 suffers from plastic charge pipe failure and oil starvation under hard use, while the B58 - widely regarded as one of BMW's best modern engines - has its own plastic component weaknesses including the oil filter housing and water pump. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Charge Pipe Failure - Why the BMW 2 Series M235i/M240i N55 Engine Loses Boost
problems.affectedModels: BMW 2 Series M235i (N55B30, 2014-2016) - predecessor to M240i
problems.rootCause: The N55's plastic charge pipe is notoriously prone to cracking under boost pressure. The OEM charge pipes used on the N55 engine are plastic, which becomes brittle and weak after time and repeated heat cycles. Once the charge pipe cracks, the engine loses boost pressure, triggering a drivetrain malfunction warning.

repairOptions.longevity: Effective; upgraded unit eliminates future failure
Required if boost loss has caused engine damage

problems.recommendation: Charge pipe failure is a well-known weakness on the N55. Upgrading to an aluminium charge pipe is a relatively inexpensive fix that prevents future failure. If the engine has suffered catastrophic boost-related damage, a rebuilt engine with upgraded components is the safest option.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt N55B30 BMW 2 Series M240i engine prices

problems.h4: Plastic Oil Filter Housing Cracking - BMW 2 Series M240i B58 Coolant and Oil Leaks
problems.rootCause: BMW's redesign for the clean-sheet B58 straight-six included an oil filter housing made from plastic, which has been prone to becoming brittle, cracking, and leaking oil, coolant, or both. The housing tends to split if the cap is tightened too tight or even just over time as the plastic becomes brittle from numerous heat cycles. This is a known potentially catastrophic problem if left unchecked.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove intake manifold, replace housing with upgraded metal unit
repairOptions.longevity: Effective; upgraded metal units don't fail again

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Pressure test, inspect for additional leaks

repairOptions.longevity: If oil/coolant mixing has caused internal damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For a typical £18,000-£45,000 M240i, oil filter housing replacement is a worthwhile repair. Full engine replacement is rarely needed for this failure alone, unless oil-coolant mixing (the "milkshake" effect) has caused bearing damage.
problems.recommendation: Oil filter housing cracking is a well-documented issue on B58 engines. Replacing the plastic housing with an upgraded metal unit is the definitive fix. If you notice coolant loss, oil contamination, or a sweet smell from the engine bay, have the housing inspected immediately.
problems.cta: -> Get quotes for BMW 2 Series M240i oil filter housing repair

problems.h4: Water Pump Failure - BMW 2 Series M240i B58 Overheating
problems.rootCause: The electric water pump on B58 engines is known to fail prematurely, which can lead to overheating. Preventative replacement around 100,000 km (62,000 miles) is recommended.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace electric water pump and thermostat
Replace pump, thermostat, hoses, expansion tank
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if multiple cooling components have failed
Required if overheating has caused head gasket failure

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For a typical £18,000-£45,000 M240i, water pump replacement is a minor expense relative to vehicle value. Full engine replacement is rarely needed for water pump failure alone, unless overheating has caused secondary damage.
problems.recommendation: Water pump failure is a known issue on B58 engines. If you notice the temperature gauge rising or the engine running hot, have the cooling system inspected immediately. Preventative replacement at 60,000-80,000 miles is advisable.
problems.cta: -> Get quotes for BMW 2 Series M240i water pump replacement

problems.h4: Oil Starvation - BMW 2 Series M235i N55 Engine Under Hard Cornering
problems.affectedModels: BMW 2 Series M235i (N55B30, 2014-2016) - predecessor to M240i
problems.typicalFailureMileage: Track use or sustained hard driving - can occur at any mileage
problems.rootCause: It's well documented that N55 BMW turbo motors can suffer from oil control problems. Under sustained high-G cornering, oil can surge away from the oil pickup, leading to momentary oil pressure loss and potential bearing damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Inspect oil pump, bearings, oil pressure
repairOptions.longevity: Required if oil pressure warning appears

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Strip, inspect, replace bearings and damaged components
repairOptions.longevity: Required if oil starvation has caused bearing failure

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For a typical M235i worth £10,000-£18,000, a baffled sump is a worthwhile preventative investment if you track the car. Full engine replacement is rarely needed unless oil starvation has caused catastrophic bearing failure.
problems.recommendation: If you track your M235i or drive it hard on B-roads, a baffled sump is a wise investment. If you've experienced an oil pressure warning, have the engine inspected immediately - bearing damage can escalate quickly.
problems.cta: -> Get quotes for BMW 2 Series M240i engine diagnostics

finalCta.h4: Don't Let Engine Failure Write Off Your BMW 2 Series M240i
finalCta.paragraph: The M240i's N55 and B58 straight-six engines are among BMW's finest, but plastic component failures - charge pipes on the N55, oil filter housings and water pumps on the B58 - can escalate quickly if ignored. With rebuilt engines available from £3,000, a 12-month warranty on every unit, and nationwide delivery and fit options, replacing your M240i engine through EnginesMarket is often more cost-effective than main dealer repairs.
